items.stem: The graph of y = 1/x has:
choices: Vertical asymptote x = 0 and horizontal asymptote y = 0
items.note: The reciprocal function: two branches, undefined at x = 0, approaching both axes but never touching them.

items.stem: Replacing f(x) with f(x) + 3 transforms the graph by:
items.note: OUTSIDE the brackets → vertical translation, direction as written. INSIDE → horizontal, opposite direction to what you'd expect.

items.stem: The graph of y = f(x − 2) is the graph of y = f(x) shifted:
items.note: Inside the brackets acts horizontally and opposite: f(x − 2) moves RIGHT by 2. The single most-mixed-up transformation.

items.stem: y = −f(x) transforms the graph of f by a reflection in:
items.note: Minus outside → flip y-values → x-axis reflection. Minus inside → f(−x) → y-axis reflection.

items.stem: y = f(−x) transforms the graph of f by a reflection in:
items.note: Minus INSIDE the brackets flips the x-values: (2, 5) → (−2, 5). Mirror image in the y-axis.

items.stem: y = 2f(x) transforms the graph of f by:
items.note: Multiplier OUTSIDE → vertical stretch (y-values doubled). Multiplier inside → horizontal compression by the reciprocal.

items.stem: y = f(2x) transforms the graph of f by:
choices: A vertical stretch with scale factor 2
A horizontal stretch with scale factor 2
A horizontal stretch with scale factor ½
items.note: y = f(2x) is a horizontal stretch with scale factor ½ (IB wording): the graph is squashed towards the y-axis. The horizontal scale factor is the RECIPROCAL of the number multiplying x.

items.stem: The point (2, 5) lies on y = f(x). Which point lies on y = f(x + 3)?
items.note: f(x + 3) shifts LEFT 3: new x = old x − 3 = −1, y unchanged. Transformations of points: outside changes y, inside changes x (opposite sign).

items.stem: The graph of y = 3ˣ passes through which point, and has which asymptote?
items.note: Any exponential y = aˣ passes through (0, 1) since a⁰ = 1, with the x-axis as horizontal asymptote.

items.stem: The horizontal asymptote of y = 2ˣ + 1 is:
items.note: The +1 lifts the asymptote: as x → −∞, 2ˣ → 0, so y → 1. Vertical shifts move horizontal asymptotes.

items.stem: The graph of y = log₂ x passes through:
items.note: log₂ 1 = 0 → every log curve passes through (1, 0). It's the mirror image of y = 2ˣ in y = x.

items.stem: Given f(x) = x + 1 and g(x) = x², solving f(g(x)) = 17 gives:
items.note: f(g(x)) = x² + 1 = 17 → x² = 16 → x = ±4. Two answers — quadratics always give both.

items.stem: f(x) = x² on the domain x ∈ ℝ has no inverse because:
choices: Two different inputs give the same output (it fails the horizontal line test)
items.note: f(2) = f(−2) = 4 — an inverse would need two outputs. Restrict the domain to x ≥ 0 and f⁻¹(x) = √x exists.

items.stem: For invertible f, (f ∘ f⁻¹)(x) equals:
items.note: A function and its inverse undo each other — the composition is the identity. Also true for (f⁻¹ ∘ f)(x) on f's domain.

items.stem: The solution set of x² − 5x + 6 < 0 is:
items.note: (x − 2)(x − 3) < 0: positive parabola → below zero BETWEEN the roots. Sketch the parabola — don't memorize rules.

items.retiredReason: AA HL only (odd and even functions, AHL 2.14)
items.stem: The function f(x) = x³ is classified as:
choices: Odd (symmetric by 180° rotation about the origin)
items.note: Odd: f(−x) = −f(x) → 180° rotation symmetry about the origin. Even: f(−x) = f(x) → y-axis symmetry (like x²).

items.stem: The transformation mapping y = x² onto y = −(x − 3)² + 2 is:
choices: Shift right 3, reflect in x-axis, shift up 2
Shift left 3, reflect in y-axis, shift up 2
Shift right 3, stretch vertically, shift down 2
items.note: Read vertex form inside-out: (x − 3) shifts right; the minus outside reflects in the x-axis; + 2 shifts up. Vertex lands at (3, 2).

items.stem: The vertex of y = −(x − 3)² + 2 is:
items.note: a < 0 opens downward → the vertex is a maximum at (3, 2). Two things to state: coordinates AND max/min.

items.stem: If (2, 5) is on y = f(x), the corresponding point on y = 2f(x) is:
items.note: Outside multiplier doubles y-values only: (2, 10). Inside multipliers change x instead.

items.stem: The horizontal asymptote of y = 3⁻ˣ is:
items.note: 3⁻ˣ → 0 as x grows positive (decay). Direction of the asymptote matters for sketch marks.

items.stem: Let f(x) = x². (a) Describe the sequence of transformations that map f onto g(x) = −(x − 3)² + 2. (b) State the coordinates and nature of the vertex of g. (c) Write down the equation of the axis of symmetry of g.
markscheme: (a) Translation 3 right; reflection in the x-axis; translation 2 up (any valid order with reflection noted) (3)
items.tactic: Vertex form contains the whole transformation story: (x − h)² shifts right, the sign of a reflects and sets max/min, + k shifts up.

items.stem: Let f(x) = 2ˣ. (a) Find f(3) − f(0). (b) Solve 2ˣ = 1/8.
markscheme: Working shown equating powers of the same base (1)
items.tactic: Exponential equations: rewrite both sides with the same base. f(0) = 1 for every exponential — a free fact on Paper 1.
